Revisiting Kulkarni’s topological proof of Millington’s theorem

Chapter

Full-text available

  * Jan 2025

  * Devendra Tiwari
  * Harshavardhan Reddy

In this work, we will revisit Ravi Kulkarni’s topological proof [Bull. London Math. Soc. 17 (1985) 458–462] of Millington’s theorem [J. London Math. Soc. 1 (1969), 351–357] on subgroups of the modular group PSL ⁡ ( 2 , Z ) \operatorname {PSL}(2, \mathbb {Z}) . Millington’s original proof was algebraic and used permutation representation methods. In particular, we simplify Kulkarni’s proof by constructing a combinatorial complex for a given finite index subgroup, which is an analogue of a dessin d’enfant . We shall also discuss Millington’s question about realizable cusp-widths of a finite index subgroup of PSL ⁡ ( 2 , Z ) \operatorname {PSL}(2, \mathbb {Z}) and briefly describe an approach to compute cusp-widths of a given finite index subgroup.

## 35.1 \(\triangleright \) The fundamental set

### Definition 35.1.1

The classical modular group is the subgroup of \({{\,\mathrm{PSL}\,}}_2(\mathbb R )\) defined by

$$\begin{aligned} {{\,\mathrm{PSL}\,}}_2(\mathbb Z )=\left\{ \gamma =\begin{pmatrix} a &{} b \\ c &{} d \end{pmatrix} : a,b,c,d \in \mathbb Z , ad-bc=1\right\} /\{\pm 1\}. \end{aligned}$$

The group \({{\,\mathrm{PSL}\,}}_2(\mathbb Z )\) acts faithfully on the upper half-plane \({\mathbf {\mathsf{{H}}}}^2\) by linear fractional transformations; equipping \({\mathbf {\mathsf{{H}}}}^2\) with the hyperbolic metric, this action is by orientation-preserving isometries.

Since \(\mathbb Z \subseteq \mathbb R \) is discrete, so too is \({{\,\mathrm{SL}\,}}_2(\mathbb Z ) \subseteq {{\,\mathrm{M}\,}}_2(\mathbb Z ) \subseteq {{\,\mathrm{M}\,}}_2(\mathbb R )\) discrete and therefore \({{\,\mathrm{PSL}\,}}_2(\mathbb Z ) \le {{\,\mathrm{PSL}\,}}_2(\mathbb R )\) is a Fuchsian group (Definition 34.7.3).
